artistic_choices: Selected documented duck transformation, excluding infant, cow and dog variants. Natural firefly light is c03, no aura.
Physical breakup into insects visually separates spirit from ordinary duck. Adult legs, path, moon and dark plumage are editorial framing. No literal death depicted.

rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.

root_visual_review.notes: Viewed native 1254px, 200px, and crops of the underside/foot, the head and the rooster. Diffed against the edit reference attempt-01: the changes are concentrated at the duck's underside and legs. This edit answers the r04 reject. The duck now has exactly ONE orange leg, ending in one webbed, clawed foot that slaps the wet mud and throws droplets in a lurching one-footed rush. On the other side there are only continuous feathers above open air and mud: no stump, wound, hidden second foot or extra toe. That is the duck missing one leg in the majimun-c04 source quote, and c04 is now in the anatomy requirement. One duck head with two eyes and a bill. One wing is raised, and the other wing and the rear body physically break apart into a swarm of individually drawn fireflies (c03). The ankle-level camera sits in the gap between two opaque trousered adult legs and boots as the duck rushes to pass between them (c02). A small rooster stands on a rise under the full moon (c03), above a wet earthen path. No gore, victim, monster teeth, text or aura; the firefly light is the documented transformation. At 200px the charging one-legged duck, dissolving into fireflies between a person's legs, is uncanny and threatening, not an ordinary farmyard duck. Limitation: the rooster is small and its call cannot be seen; it serves as a setting cue.
